# Generating images with Codex

`codex` ships an `image_gen` tool. It runs on the machine's ChatGPT login, so
nothing here needs `OPENAI_API_KEY` and no key is written anywhere.

This skill owns producing a **bitmap file**. It does not own how the page looks
or behaves — `kx-design` and `kx-ux` do. An icon that has to match an SVG set
the repo already has is an edit to those files, not a generated PNG.

## First, check the machine has it

Three things, in this order. Each one fails differently and the message the
tool gives is not always the reason:

```bash
command -v codex || echo "not installed"
codex login status
codex features list | grep '^image_generation'
```

- **No `codex` on PATH.** Nothing here works. Say so and stop — do not fall
  back to writing an SVG and calling it the asset that was asked for.
- **`Logged in using ChatGPT`** is the working state. Anything else — not
  logged in, or an API-key login — and the generation fails partway through a
  turn that has already cost time. `codex login` fixes the first.
- **`image_generation … true`** is the flag. It is `stable`, but a machine
  whose `config.toml` disabled it reports `false`, and the agent then
  improvises an SVG instead of erroring. Read the third column.

Verified against `codex-cli 0.153.4`.

## The invocation

```bash
cd <destination directory>
codex exec --skip-git-repo-check -s workspace-write --json \
  --output-schema schema.json -o result.json \
  "Genera … Guárdala como hero.png en el directorio de trabajo.
   Devuelve el JSON con la ruta absoluta y las dimensiones reales,
   comprobadas con \`file\`." \
  < /dev/null > run.jsonl 2>&1
```

**`< /dev/null` is not optional.** With stdin left open `codex exec` prints
`Reading additional input from stdin...` and waits — forever, with the process
alive, no output and no image. It looks exactly like a slow generation. Ten
minutes were lost to it once.

`-s workspace-write` is what lets it write the file at all. `--skip-git-repo-check`
makes the line work outside a repository as well as inside one.

**Name the destination filename in the prompt.** The tool writes to its own
directory and the agent copies from there; if nothing names a destination the
copy never happens and the asset stays outside the project.

## Getting the path back

Use `--output-schema` with `-o`, and read the file:

```json
{
  "type": "object", "additionalProperties": false, "required": ["images"],
  "properties": { "images": { "type": "array", "items": {
    "type": "object", "additionalProperties": false,
    "required": ["name", "path", "width", "height"],
    "properties": { "name": {"type": "string"}, "path": {"type": "string"},
                    "width": {"type": "integer"}, "height": {"type": "integer"} } } } }
}
```

**The JSONL carries no event for the image.** In `--json` the only trace is the
`command_execution` of the `cp`; the tool call itself is invisible. A parser
built on the event stream finds nothing.

If the run ends without saying where the file went, it is at
`${CODEX_HOME:-$HOME/.codex}/generated_images/<thread_id>/exec-<uuid>.png`,
where `thread_id` is in the `thread.started` event on the first line.

## What you ask for and what you get

| Asked | Got |
|---|---|
| default | 1254×1254 |
| "apaisada 16:9" | 1664×936 |
| "fondo transparente" | RGBA with real alpha — corner α=0 |

Aspect is a request in the prompt and it is honoured. **Exact pixel dimensions
are not**, and neither are model, quality or `input_fidelity`. Those exist only
on the fallback path — `$CODEX_HOME/skills/.system/imagegen/scripts/image_gen.py`
— which does need `OPENAI_API_KEY` and bills separately. Do not switch to it to
get a size; resize the PNG.

Read the file back before reporting it done. `file x.png` gives the real
dimensions, and the image itself is the only check on whether the prompt worked.

## Editing an image the repo already has

Same command, pointed at the file. Fidelity is high: recolouring a flat-vector
fox from orange to blue kept every shape identical and changed only the hue —
identical in shape, not in pixels. When untouched pixels must match the source,
see the next section.

Say what must not change — `cambia SOLO el color del pelaje, mantén todo lo
demás idéntico` — and write to a new filename. It will not overwrite an
existing asset unless told to.

## Changing one region of an image

For an inpaint-style edit — one object changes, every other pixel stays — the
model has no mask. It re-renders the whole frame, so pixels outside the edit
drift even when the prompt says not to touch them. Keep the region from the
model and everything else from the source:

1. Prompt `codex exec` as in the edit above, naming one object:
   `change ONLY <object>, keep everything else identical`. Write to a new
   filename. Ask for the source's aspect, so the resize in step 2 only scales
   and the edit stays over its region.
2. Resize the output to the source's exact size. It comes back at one of the
   sizes in the table above, not yours.
3. Composite in a script: build your own mask for the region (white where the
   edit goes, black elsewhere), then take edited pixels inside it and source
   pixels outside, e.g. with `sharp`. Feather the edge a pixel or two if it
   shows.

Read the result back against the source. Anything that differs outside the
feathered mask is a bug in the script, not in the model. Check the seam at the
mask edge too, not only the pixels outside it.

**Do not use `image_gen.py --mask`**, although it supports masks. It is the
fallback path: it needs `OPENAI_API_KEY` and bills the org, and a batch of
region edits stopped mid-run on `429 credit_balance_exhausted` that way.

## Cost, and why there is no wrapper script here

One image is roughly one minute and one full Codex turn — about 90k input
tokens, most of them cached, on the **ChatGPT quota, not the calling agent's
context**. Three in one session took 210 s; two `codex exec` in parallel took
90 s and did not collide, which is the faster shape for a batch.

Telling it to skip reading its own instructions to save tokens was measured and
made it **worse** (92.8k → 106.3k): the generated image dominates the context,
the prompt text is a rounding error. Nothing a wrapper could do changes the
number that matters, it would save the caller about two hundred tokens of bash,
and `pnpm sync` copies skill files as text with default permissions — a script
would arrive non-executable and have to be called through `bash` anyway. The
one failure worth preventing is `< /dev/null`, and that is a flag, not a
program.
